objections.claim: The spec places the emission in `dodClassify` ("emit each `doneHeadingWarnings` string via `process.stderr.write(...)`"). But `dodClassify` is not `dod classify`'s private engine — it is called internally by `proseDoneAdvisory`, `oracleLessAdvisory`, `codeSurfaceAdvisory`, and `scenariosCodeSurfaceAdvisory`, all of which run on every `faff admissible --lights-out` invocation. Emitting at the classify-engine layer means `faff admissible` prints the new `dod classify: ...` warnings — up to four times per run (once per internal `dodClassify` call) — exactly the triple-print the spec's out-of-scope item ("emitting it from three commands would triple-print") and its design decision ("keep `parseDoneChecklist` pure; warn from `dod classify`") claim to have avoided. The emission point, not the purity, is what violates the scoping decision.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 HOW procedure `dod_classify_with_warning` step 2, and the "Design decision — keep `parseDoneChecklist` pure; warn from `dod classify`" paragraph; in the supplied `admissibility.js`, `proseDoneAdvisory`/`oracleLessAdvisory`/`codeSurfaceAdvisory`/`scenariosCodeSurfaceAdvisory` each call `dodClassify(specText)`.
objections.predicted_consequence: `faff admissible --lights-out` on a near-miss-shaped spec emits the dod-classify-branded warning repeatedly on stderr — and `faff admissible --selftest` fixtures whose stderr is captured will show phantom `dod classify:` lines — while the spec simultaneously asserts the warning is scoped to `dod classify` only.

objections.claim: The failure-modes section names `## Done and dusted: the retro` as a residual mis-recognition (a leading-"done" body heading), and says "proceed — the warning is the designed-in safety net". But the safety net cannot fire for this case: `doneHeadingWarnings` only warns about headings **not** recognised as DONE that contain "done", and `## Done and dusted…` **is** recognised (leading word "done"), so its checklist items are silently classified as DONE criteria with no warning at all. The spec's stated mitigation does not apply to the exact scenario it invokes it for; "a confirmed bad case narrows the regex in a follow-up" is the honest deferral, but the sentence claiming the warning covers it is factually wrong as written.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 failure modes, first bullet ("the leading-word anchor is still too loose … `## Done and dusted: the retro` is wrongly treated as the DONE section … the warning is the designed-in safety net"); the `doneHeadingWarnings` pseudocode only emits for `NOT isDoneHeading(h.text)`.
objections.predicted_consequence: A builder or reviewer reading the failure-modes section relies on the warning to surface the "Done and dusted" mis-parse, gets none, and the spec's own defect-detection narrative fails on first contact with the named case; the fix is a one-sentence correction, but as written the safety-net claim is false.

objections.claim: `doneHeadingWarnings` is specified to emit warnings "naming that heading" — i.e. the heading text itself, which is attacker-influenced spec content in any lane where a spec is authored by an agent or imported from outside the repo. The file's existing advisory idiom (`renderProseDoneWarning`, `renderCodeSurfaceWarning`, `renderOracleLessWarning`, and the R2b detail) deliberately whitespace-collapses and truncates to ~50 chars before printing; the new warnings carry no truncation, collapsing, or escaping requirement. Unbounded spec-controlled text written to stderr can poison captured logs, break line-oriented log parsers, and smuggle fake `dod classify:`-prefixed lines into an operator's transcript (a line beginning `dod classify:` followed by attacker-chosen text is indistinguishable from a genuine advisory in most log aggregation).
objections.evidence: `## 3. WHAT`, ambiguity-detector pseudocode — `warnings.push("dod classify: checklist items under a heading not recognised as DONE (<h.text>) — rename it...")` and `"more than one DONE section heading — using the first (<first>); also saw <others>"`; contrast the truncating idiom in `renderProseDoneWarning` / `renderCodeSurfaceWarning` in the module under review.
objections.predicted_consequence: an arbitrarily long or multi-line-shaped heading string from a spec under review is written verbatim into the run's captured stderr, letting spec content forge additional `dod classify:` advisory lines or flood the log.

objections.claim: The spec presents the shared-predicate narrowing as fixing both the DONE start-match and the "Scenarios over-stop" simultaneously, but never analyses what happens to the Scenarios section content that the over-stop used to exclude. After the fix, on exactly the spec shape this ticket targets (`### The trust shift for prose DONE items` before `## 7. DONE — Definition of Done`), `sectionBodyRange`'s boundary walk no longer stops at the near-miss heading — it now runs the Scenarios body all the way to the real DONE heading. That body now *contains* the near-miss heading line and any prose paragraphs under it, and `classifyAcceptanceCriteria` turns every such line into a criterion: the heading line matches none of the skip rules (blank / italic-placeholder / blockquote / bullet / `Given`), so it lands as a `source:"scenarios"`, `class:"prose"` phantom criterion — which per FAFF-1291 is tiered `running-stack` with `verifier:"holdout"`, i.e. the code-blind holdout is handed a criterion that is literally a section heading. The pre-fix behaviour excluded this content; the post-fix behaviour invents it, on the ticket's own motivating case, and the spec's three-edit plan, failure-mode analysis, and DONE items never mention it.
objections.evidence: Spec §1 "Design principle — one recogniser, three callers … Narrowing it in place simultaneously fixes the `dod classify` start-match and the Scenarios over-stop"; §4 "Three edits in `admissibility.js`, all in the recogniser block"; and the supplied `admissibility.js` where `scenariosBoundaryStop` (the only DONE-keyed Scenarios stop) calls `isDoneHeading`, and `classifyAcceptanceCriteria` promotes any non-blank, non-bullet, non-`Given` body line to a unit ("a bare leading prose/assertion line").
objections.predicted_consequence: Running the spec's own smoke-test spec shape through `faff dod classify` post-fix returns the two DONE items **plus** one or more new phantom `scenarios:*` prose criteria (the near-miss heading text and intervening prose), which flow into `judged_count`, into the holdout's judged set as a heading-shaped criterion, and into `dod split`/`admissible` counts — a new wrong-output regression introduced by the fix for the hidden-DONE bug, undetectable by any of the spec's planned selftest assertions.

objections.claim: The rationale section's resolution of "Where does the ambiguity warning live?" states the chosen option as "a pure `doneHeadingWarnings(specText)` helper **emitted by `dodClassify`**", while §3's design decision, the HOW procedure, and the DONE item all mandate emission from the `cmdDod` command layer precisely because emitting from `dodClassify` leaks the `dod classify:`-branded warning into `faff admissible` (via `proseDoneAdvisory` / `oracleLessAdvisory` / `codeSurfaceAdvisory` / `scenariosCodeSurfaceAdvisory`) and violates the scoped-to-`dod-classify` AC. A builder resolving the ambiguity from §6 alone implements the leaky option.
objections.evidence: §3 "Design decision — keep both pure functions pure; emit the warning from the `cmdDod` command layer"; DONE item "The new warnings are emitted from the `cmdDod` command layer, not from `dodClassify`"; versus §6 "**Chosen:** a pure `doneHeadingWarnings(specText)` helper emitted by `dodClassify`."
objections.predicted_consequence: A builder following §6's "Chosen" line ships the warning inside `dodClassify`, and `faff admissible` prints up to four `dod classify:` stderr lines per run — the exact cross-command leak the AC forbids — failing the DONE item "…`faff admissible` … prints none of them".

objections.claim: The spec correctly identifies heading text as attacker-influenceable spec content and mandates that every interpolated heading pass through the whitespace-collapse-and-truncate idiom before reaching stderr. That idiom (as the spec itself describes it: "collapse every whitespace run (incl. newlines) to a single space, then truncate to ~60 chars") neutralises log-line forging and flooding but does nothing about ANSI/CSI escape sequences embedded in the heading. A spec heading such as `## DONE\x1b[2J\x1b[?25l…` — or one crafted to move the cursor and overwrite prior output — passes through collapse-and-truncate intact and is emitted raw by `cmdDod`'s new `process.stderr.write(w + "\n")`. The threat is reached by any untrusted contributor able to write a spec heading that flows through `faff dod classify` in a captured or TTY-attached transcript.
objections.evidence: "Heading text is untrusted" paragraph in `### 3. WHAT`, which claims the idiom "stops a multi-line or overlong heading from forging extra `dod classify:` log lines or flooding a captured transcript" — it claims line-forging safety, not control-character safety, and the new emission point in `### 4. HOW` (`process.stderr.write(w + "\n")`) prints the resulting string verbatim.
objections.predicted_consequence: Terminal escape injection into the stderr stream of `faff dod classify` runs (and any CI log that captures it) from a malicious spec heading — cosmetic-to-moderate: overwritten log lines, hidden text in captured transcripts. No privilege or data impact.

objections.claim: The detector fires on any heading that contains "done", is not recognised as a DONE heading, and has checklist items under it — with no exclusion for headings nested *within* the recognised DONE section. For such a heading the items ARE already classified (parseDoneChecklist includes sub-headings under the DONE heading), yet the warning asserts the opposite.
objections.evidence: `doneHeadingWarnings` pseudocode in "The ambiguity detector" (### 3. WHAT); the warning string "rename it to a DONE heading (e.g. '## DONE') so its items are classified". Concrete shape: `## 7. DONE — Definition of Done` followed by `### Items already done` with `- [ ]` items beneath it — the sub-heading contains "done", is not a DONE heading by the new regex, has checklist items, so the warning fires even though every item under it is classified.
objections.predicted_consequence: `faff dod classify` emits a warning whose advice ("so its items are classified") is false for that spec, training operators to ignore the warning — the exact trust erosion the advisory channel exists to avoid. A selftest over this shape would currently fail only by accident of fixture choice; the spec's fixtures never place a "done"-containing sub-heading inside the DONE section.
